How life has changed in Hinckley and Bosworth: Census 2021


Hinckley and Bosworth's population increased by around 8,600 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.


Select an alternative area


19 January 2023


The population passed 110,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Hinckley and Bosworth increased by 8.1%, from around 105,100 in 2011 to around 113,600 in 2021.

The population here increased at a similar rate to the overall population of the East Midlands (7.7%), but by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Hinckley and Bosworth was home to around 2.7 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 2.5 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 40% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Hinckley and Bosworth than across the East Midlands

An older Hinckley and Bosworth

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Hinckley and Bosworth increased by two years, from 43 to 45 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the East Midlands as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 3,200 (an increase of 30.3%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 2,000 (8.5% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 2.1 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Changing relationships in Hinckley and Bosworth

Hinckley and Bosworth saw the East Midlands' joint third-largest percentage-point rise (alongside Melton, South Holland and West Lindsey) in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership (from 9.3% in 2011 to 10.1% in 2021).

Across the region, only North East Derbyshire (from 9.2% to 10.3%) and South Kesteven (from 9.9% to 10.8%) saw a greater increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership.

Across the East Midlands, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 9.3% to 9.5%, while the percentage in nearby Blaby increased from 8.7% to 8.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

Rise in private renting

In 2021, 14.4% of Hinckley and Bosworth households rented privately. This figure increased from 11.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 households (10.2%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 10.3% in 2011. The percentage of Hinckley and Bosworth households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 76.7% to 74.4%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater across the East Midlands (3.8 percentage points, from 14.9% to 18.7%) than in Hinckley and Bosworth (3.0 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Unpaid care in Hinckley and Bosworth

In 2021, 5.0% of Hinckley and Bosworth residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.7% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Hinckley and Bosworth (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East Midlands (2.8 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

Religion in Hinckley and Bosworth

In 2021, 41.7% of Hinckley and Bosworth residents reported having "No religion", up from 26.9% in 2011. The rise of 14.8 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Hinckley and Bosworth. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.5% to 40.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 49.8% of people in Hinckley and Bosworth described themselves as Christian (down from 64.3%), while 5.3% did not state their religion (down from 6.5% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Hinckley and Bosworth residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 104,200 Hinckley and Bosworth residents said they were born in England. This represented 91.7% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 98,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 93.6% of Hinckley and Bosworth's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with around 1,200 Hinckley and Bosworth residents reporting this country of birth (1.1%). This figure has remained relatively unchanged from 2011.

The number of Hinckley and Bosworth residents born in Poland rose from around 300 in 2011 (0.3% of the local population) to just over 1,000 in 2021 (0.9%).

Health in Hinckley and Bosworth

In 2021, 47.9% of Hinckley and Bosworth residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 46.3% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.7% to 35.2%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Hinckley and Bosworth residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 1.0%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.7% to 3.5%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

National identity in Hinckley and Bosworth

In 2021, 3.5% of Hinckley and Bosworth residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.1% in 2011.

In 2021, 0.9% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.3% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Hinckley and Bosworth that identified as "British only" increased from 13.2% to 54.0%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the East Midlands (2.7 percentage points, from 5.8% to 8.5%) than in Hinckley and Bosworth (1.4 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

Fewer couples without children

Of Hinckley and Bosworth households, 19.9% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 22.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in five households (19.3%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 20.0% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children decreased from 6.9% to 6.6%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Hinckley and Bosworth (2.1 percentage points) than across the East Midlands (1.3 percentage points, from 19.5% to 18.2%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

Change in employment

Of Hinckley and Bosworth residents aged 16 years and over, 58.4% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 60.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.9%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.8% in 2011. The percentage of retired Hinckley and Bosworth residents increased from 24.4% to 26.6%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Hinckley and Bosworth (2.4 percentage points) than across the East Midlands (1.0 percentage points, from 56.1% to 55.1%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

Working hours in Hinckley and Bosworth

In 2021, 9.0% of Hinckley and Bosworth residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was the same in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in nine people (11.0%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 13.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 58.3% to 61.1%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week remained 9.8% across the East Midlands. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

Disability in Hinckley and Bosworth

In 2021, 6.5% of Hinckley and Bosworth residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.6% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.5%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.6% in 2011. The proportion of Hinckley and Bosworth residents who were not disabled increased from 82.8% to 83.0%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across the East Midlands (1.6 percentage points, from 9.3% to 7.7%) than in Hinckley and Bosworth (1.1 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

Ethnic groups in Hinckley and Bosworth

In 2021, 1.8% of Hinckley and Bosworth residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 1.0% in 2011. The 0.8 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East Midlands, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 1.9% to 2.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 94.3% of people in Hinckley and Bosworth identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 96.5% in 2011), while 2.8% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 2.1% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.2% in 2011 to 0.6% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

About the data

Census data are adjusted to reflect estimated non-response so that the published results relate to the entire usually resident population as it was on Census Day (21 March 2021).

Those respondents who were on furlough because of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic were asked to classify themselves as "temporarily away from work" to ensure they remained in the economically active population.

Students are counted as usually resident at their term-time address even if they were not physically present there on Census Day.

The questions relating to disability differed slightly between 2011 and 2021 to ensure that data were more closely aligned with the definition of disability in the Equality Act (2010). There was also a change to question wording for unpaid care, for more information read the health, disability and unpaid care quality information.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout the health, disability and unpaid care sections. They allow for fairer comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure. The 2013 European Standard Population is used to standardise proportions.

Percentages and percentage point changes have been individually rounded to one decimal place. This means they may not sum exactly.

About these articles

There is an article like this for every local authority district in England and Wales. The articles have been written and semi-automated by our data journalists and are a new publishing format for the Office for National Statistics.

Topics are chosen and ordered automatically based on how relevant they are for each area, however all data are checked before publishing.

We have not included topics that were new for Census 2021 or where there is no comparability with the 2011 Census. Read about how we developed and tested the questions for Census 2021.

These articles were first published on 8 December 2022 covering topics such as demography, country of birth, ethnic groups, religion, national identity and economic activity status. They were updated on 19 January 2023 following the release of more data from Census 2021 and now include housing tenure, general health, disability and unpaid care.
